outputs: Generated responses to prompts for everyday tasks, such as summarizing articles, suggesting recipes, grouping students, writing code, and editing text

The paper evaluates LLM-generated outputs across 30 everyday tasks involving decision-making with implicit values, such as copyediting emails, selecting travel plans, suggesting recipes, and writing code.

changes_made.explanation: No changes needed - all extracted metadata is accurate and properly normalized
The paper does not use automatic NLG evaluation metrics. It uses statistical tests (Fisher's Exact Test, Kruskal-Wallis Test) to compare distributions, but these are not NLG evaluation metrics.
No LLMs were used as judges/evaluators in this study. The LLMs were only used as generators.

guideline: Participants completed all 30 tasks (plus two attention checks) in randomized order
Responses were collected through Qualtrics survey platform with constrained response formats
100 human crowdworkers from the US completed the same 30 tasks as the LLMs
Statistical comparison was performed between human and LLM responses to assess alignment of implicit values
